_about: Disclosure map for the Try SES teaser 'The Study That Stalled'. Source: SES Teaser spec (JMD, 20 Nov 2026), 'Disclosure map: the four teaser items' and the teaser SIC key. chunk_ids must match alex_martinez_teaser_sic_key.json exactly. The router classifies a student turn against these items; policy.py decides what Alex may say.
assigned_goal: Find out what has happened between the 2018 Downtown Waterfront Resilience Feasibility Study's recommendations and action, and why.

items.label: The formal path
items.general_answer: Gives it readily: council approval, outside grants, state and federal permits for shoreline work, phasing.
items.targeted_answer: Adds that the phases were sized to fit what grants could fund.
cues: Why hasn't it been built?
What would it take to move the plan forward?
How does a project like this get approved or funded?
Asks about permits, grants, council approval or phasing

items.label: Staff time
items.targeted_answer: A small department. Nuisance-flood coordination, permitting and grant reporting fill the time that would move a multi-year capital program, and it's the same people doing both.
cues: Asks about staffing, bandwidth or coordination load
Acknowledges that adaptation work competes with day-to-day operations
Picks up Alex's mention of the Public Works coordination meeting and asks about it
Asks what Alex's own week looks like when it floods
Picks up the word 'capacity'

items.label: What can win approval
items.general_answer: Not offered beyond "that's ultimately a council decision."
items.targeted_answer: Council support gathers around steps that are incremental and reversible. A multi-phase commitment outlasts election cycles. Construction downtown in peak season and a large upfront cost are harder to defend than long-term uncertainty. So the package moved as smaller pieces.
cues: Asks what makes a project easier or harder to approve
Asks what enables vs. constrains decisions politically
Introduces 'phasing' or 'sequencing' rather than 'when will you act'
Probes how the planner navigates competing constituencies
Asks why the plan moved as smaller pieces rather than as a whole

items.label: What a wall would promise
items.targeted_answer: Only indirectly. A big visible wall signals a permanence nobody can promise; it may draw more investment into exposed areas; and a success story can postpone harder conversations. Some of the slowness reflects her own professional caution, not only obstacles.
items.allowed_restraint: May decline to say whether the full plan should be built and redirect to its assumptions; this is appropriate professional restraint, not a failure.
cues: Paraphrases the 'buying time' tension before probing
Asks 'how do you think about' rather than 'will this work'
Opens the gap between visible investment and the assumptions it rests on
Frames questions around durability, lifespan or longevity rather than effectiveness
Probes whether short-term wins might create lock-in or false reassurance
Asks whether some of the caution reflects Alex's own professional judgment, without implying blame
not_a_cue: Asks for a verdict: 'Should they build it?', 'Would it work?'
